items.title: Caught in the Act
items.credit: Photo by Tony Wu for National Geographic
items.subject: Moray eels releasing gametes. Nat Geo says no human on record had photographed eels spawning in the wild before Wu.
items.lesson: Patience and gentle light. The team spent hundreds of hours underwater since 2023 for an act that lasts less than two seconds, using faint red light that did not spook the fish.
items.tpm_idea: Reel or carousel: "Would you wait hundreds of hours for 2 seconds?" A post on anticipation and patience in wildlife work.

items.title: Realm of the Zombie Sharks
items.credit: Photo by Kiliii Yüyan for National Geographic
items.subject: A juvenile Greenland shark swims past Yüyan and dive partner Philipp Oppermann under the sea ice.
items.lesson: Teamwork and safety make extreme shoots possible. His team on the ice pulled his dive line when they spotted a polar bear.
items.tpm_idea: Behind the scenes story post: "The crew you don't see", on planning, spotters and safety for risky locations.

items.title: Open Wide
items.credit: Photo by Ralph Pace for National Geographic
items.subject: A whale lunges, mouth agape, to feed on krill in New Zealand's warming waters.
items.lesson: Access through experts. Pace dived with researchers studying how climate change affects the krill and the whales.
items.tpm_idea: Tip post: "Partner with scientists, guides or locals to get the shot and the story."

items.title: Pearls of the Pond
items.credit: Photo by Shane Gross for National Geographic
items.subject: Two American toads spawn among strands of eggs arrayed like beads on a necklace, in Ontario's Experimental Lakes Area.
items.lesson: Pattern and repetition. The strands of eggs turn a small subject into a strong graphic frame.
items.tpm_idea: Weekly challenge: "Find a pattern in nature" with the TPM community sharing their own shots.

items.title: A Flourish in Flight
items.credit: Photo by Jaime Rojo for National Geographic
items.subject: A male resplendent quetzal in flight in Mexico's El Triunfo Biosphere Reserve.
items.lesson: Fieldcraft. Rojo spent 10 days in a blind before getting this shot.
items.tpm_idea: Carousel: "Birds in flight, a beginner's guide" covering blinds, patience and shutter speed basics.

items.title: Monkey Business
items.credit: Photo by Prakash Matada for National Geographic
items.subject: A troop of endangered Gee's golden langurs peer into a fisheye lens Matada fixed to a telescoping pole.
items.lesson: Creative camera placement. A wide lens on a pole puts the viewer right inside the troop.
items.tpm_idea: Perspective tip: "Go wide and close", showing how lens choice and camera position change the story.

items.title: Animal Crossing
items.credit: Photo by Will Burrard-Lucas for National Geographic
items.subject: Lions slink through a hidden riverbank crossing, caught on a camera trap set with a team of rangers.
items.lesson: Camera traps reveal what you would never see in person. He set out for black rhino and also recorded elephants, leopards, hippos and more.
items.tpm_idea: Explainer: "Camera traps 101", what they are and why pros use them.

items.title: Busy Bees
items.credit: Photo by Anand Varma for National Geographic
items.subject: Three common eastern bumblebees on beeswax cells inside an acrylic box designed by Nat Geo Explorer Felicity Muth.
items.lesson: A controlled setup can show hidden behavior. Macro plus a purpose built set tells a science story.
items.tpm_idea: Macro at home post: simple ways to build a small set for insects, flowers or products.

items.title: A Hard Day's Rest
items.credit: Photo by Matthieu Paley for National Geographic
items.subject: Hazal-u Din reclines by firelight after a long day herding yaks.
items.lesson: Trust over time and a single warm light. Paley first visited the region 26 years ago and keeps returning.
items.tpm_idea: Portrait lesson: "One light source", using firelight, a lamp or a window for mood.

items.title: Foraging Ahead
items.credit: Photo by Amy Toensing for National Geographic
items.subject: 79 year old Bente Brekke Kampevold hunts for chanterelles in the woods of western Norway.
items.lesson: Everyday routines are stories. A simple daily habit becomes a story about healthy aging.
items.tpm_idea: Assignment: "Photograph someone's daily ritual" for the TPM community.

items.title: Coming to Grips
items.credit: Photo by Justin Jin for National Geographic
items.subject: Wrestlers locked in a hold during bokh at Mongolia's Naadam festival.
items.lesson: Read the tension. Nat Geo notes holds can last hours, each wrestler waiting for a shift in weight.
items.tpm_idea: Carousel: "How to shoot peak action at festivals and sports".

items.title: Fiery Advance
items.credit: Photo by Chantal Pinzi for National Geographic
items.subject: A crack of rifle fire marks the finale of a tbourida performance, a Moroccan equestrian tradition.
items.lesson: Know the climax and the bigger story. The finale gives the peak moment, and women gaining a foothold in the sport gives the meaning.
items.tpm_idea: Event photography tip: "Learn the schedule, be ready for the finale."

items.title: Unbridled Joy
items.credit: Photo by Jasper Doest for National Geographic
items.subject: Lorena Masei playfully offers her hat to a horse at her family's farm in the Italian Alps.
items.lesson: Stay open to the unplanned story. Doest came to document coexistence with wild animals and was struck by the family's bond with their livestock.
items.tpm_idea: Community prompt: "Share the shot you didn't plan."

items.title: The Night Shift
items.credit: Photo by Jason Gulley for National Geographic
items.subject: A fisherman sleeps on his bamboo and log weir beneath the Khon Pa Soi waterfall on the Mekong.
items.lesson: Juxtaposition. Stillness against churning water makes the frame, and the threat from new dams gives it weight.
items.tpm_idea: Storytelling post: "Contrast tells the story" with calm vs chaos examples.

items.title: Catching Solar Rays
items.credit: Photo by Diego López Calvín for National Geographic
items.subject: A six month solarigraph of the sun's arc over the Chankillo complex, the oldest known solar observatory in the Americas.
items.lesson: Time as a creative tool. A lensless pinhole camera and photosensitive paper recorded one band per day.
items.tpm_idea: DIY challenge: "Make a pinhole solarigraph", a low cost project that teaches light and exposure.

items.title: Total Cliff-Hanger
items.credit: Photo by Chris Burkard for National Geographic
items.subject: Climber Chris Sharma hangs from a horizontal limestone face just after August's total solar eclipse. Burkard shot with his assistant Joel Barger from a beach some 600 feet away.
items.lesson: Plan around a rare event, then add a human element. The eclipse sets the light; the climber makes the story.
items.tpm_idea: Planning post: "How to plan a shoot around an eclipse, moonrise or sunset."

items.title: Beams of Hope
items.credit: Photo by Christopher Payne for National Geographic
items.subject: Technicians set up the 9/11 Tribute in Light. Payne combined four images for this frame.
items.lesson: Honest compositing for night scenes. Combining frames can solve a lighting problem, and Nat Geo says so openly.
items.tpm_idea: Editing ethics post: "When is compositing OK? Be transparent."

items.title: Encroaching Sands
items.credit: Photo by John Stanmeyer for National Geographic
items.subject: Fifteen foot dunes threaten the home of Haruna Modu, forced to move four times as desertification spreads across the Sahel.
items.lesson: Scale makes a global issue personal. A single home against the sand shows the problem at a glance.
items.tpm_idea: Composition tip: "Show scale with one human element."

items.title: Sun, Sand, and Salt Mines
items.credit: Photo by George Steinmetz for National Geographic
items.subject: China's largest salt lake, a former industrial mining settlement now a tourist hot spot, with a Ferris wheel under construction.
items.lesson: Landscapes with a story. Tourism and industry side by side make the scene unexpected.
items.tpm_idea: Landscape lesson: "Look for the story, not just the view."
